c50_hypothesis.name: Volume Skewness Shock Mean Reversion (Volume Distribution Asymmetry Burst Fade)
c50_hypothesis.description: Compute rolling skewness (Fisher, 3rd-moment distributional asymmetry) of real quote volume over 24h, z-score over 168h (causal) -> skew_z. Fade extreme volume-asymmetry bursts: skew_z >= 1.25 and ret_W>0 -> SHORT; skew_z >= 1.25 and ret_W<0 -> LONG. Extreme left-skewed volume drought/scarcity (skew_z <= -1.25) -> no entry (pre-stated asymmetry). Exit on skew_z < 0.25, max hold 12h, or flip. Execution t->t+1. WF 720/168/168, cost grid 0-40bps, B&H benchmark on same OOS windows.
c50_hypothesis.differs_from_c23: C23 trades high vol_z LEVEL (first-moment volume z) momentum continuation; C50 uses z-score of rolling SKEWNESS of qvol (3rd-moment asymmetry) as a shock fade.
c50_hypothesis.differs_from_c40: C40 fades HIGH volume climax on aggregate vol_z level; C50 fades VOLUME DISTRIBUTION ASYMMETRY (skewness) — different transform (3rd moment asymmetry, not volume level).
c50_hypothesis.differs_from_c41: C41 continues on LOW vol_z dry-up breakout; C50 mean-reverts on extreme volume asymmetry shocks (high skew_z).
c50_hypothesis.differs_from_c42: C42 confirms breakouts on volume expansion (level); C50 uses volume skewness (distribution asymmetry) shock fade, no breakout/expansion confirmation.
c50_hypothesis.differs_from_c43: C43 fades volume-price divergence using unsloped vol_z at price extremes; C50 uses skew_z (volume distribution asymmetry) shock with ret_W confirmation — different transform and trigger.
c50_hypothesis.differs_from_c44: C44 trend-follows on vol_z ROC acceleration; C50 mean-reverts on extreme skew_z volume-asymmetry shocks, no ROC/acceleration.
c50_hypothesis.differs_from_c45: C45 mean-reverts on Amihud illiquidity shocks (|ret|/volume, price-impact ratio); C50 uses rolling skewness of qvol (distribution asymmetry), not a price-impact ratio.
c50_hypothesis.differs_from_c46: C46 continues on OBV (cumulative sign*vol) slope divergence vs price slope; C50 uses skew_z volume-asymmetry shock fade — different transform (3rd moment vs OBV slopes) and opposite mechanic.
c50_hypothesis.differs_from_c47: C47 uses up/down volume split imbalance ratio (directional partitioned sums) exhaustion fade; C50 uses rolling skewness of total qvol (undirected distribution asymmetry/3rd moment) — different construction.
c50_hypothesis.differs_from_c48: C48 uses z-score of rolling STD of qvol (2nd-moment dispersion/volatility-of-liquidity); C50 uses z-score of rolling SKEWNESS of qvol (3rd-moment distributional asymmetry) — distinct moment measuring directional bias, not dispersion magnitude.
c50_hypothesis.differs_from_c49: C49 uses z-score of rolling EXCESS KURTOSIS of qvol (4th-moment tail-fatness/spikiness); C50 uses z-score of rolling SKEWNESS of qvol (3rd-moment distributional asymmetry) — different moment statistic measuring asymmetry vs tail shape.
